A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dinomaly. All 23 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v3, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support comparison. Renumbered and relocated content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original Dinomaly benchmark results, component ablations, scaling experiments, qualitative outputs, and a five-seed analysis.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds experiments on additional datasets, component transfer to RD4AD, and further scaling and noise comparisons.

M1.justification: The core Dinomaly architecture, reconstruction objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged. v3 adds a limited procedural adaptation to CNN-based RD4AD: dropout before its MFF layer and the hard-mining Loose Loss, separately and together (Appendix 8, Table A8).

E1.justification: Beyond the retained MVTec-AD, VisA, and Real-IAD evaluations, v3 adds MPDD, BTAD, and Uni-Medical (Section 9, Table A11). These introduce additional industrial categories, BTAD training data described as contaminated, and brain, liver, and retinal medical images, substantially extending evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes EfficientAD from the class-separated comparison, although it remains represented in Figure 1. The foundation comparison adds MOCOv3 (v1 Table A4; v3 Table 6), and the noise comparison adds patch masking (v1 Table A6; v3 Table A7). Table 1's comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The established splits, training budgets, and main evaluation metrics remain. Table 2 replaces pixel AP with pixel AUROC. New studies vary baseline input resolutions and combine Dinomaly model/input sizes; Uni-Medical uses dropout 0.4. Table 6 corrects the DINOv2 crop entry from 396 to 392, matching v1's prose without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of patch masking versus dropout, NB/LL transfer to RD4AD, baseline sensitivity to input resolution, and performance versus computational cost (Tables A7–A9 and Table 5). It also extends model-scaling analysis to VisA and Real-IAD (Table A2). These substantially expand the questions tested beyond the retained, relocated ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose a single-seed default with deterministic CUDA and a separate five-seed MVTec-AD experiment. v1 Table A7 and v3 Table A10 contain identical seed results and mean±standard-deviation reporting. No additional uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial benchmark and analytical results, including image AUROCs of 97.2, 95.4, and 84.9 on MPDD, BTAD, and Uni-Medical. It changes no-noise AUROC from 98.19 to 99.19 and revises Table 2's VisA image AUROCs for PatchCore from 95.1 to 94.7 and SimpleNet from 96.8 to 97.1. Table 1 and all six per-class tables remain unchanged. Table 2's AP-to-AUROC replacement is not a performance gain.

T1.justification: The attention derivations and hard-mining cosine objective retain their mathematical substance. v3 introduces clearer intermediate-feature notation and writes the retained threshold as k%; its appendix preserves the same warm-up to 90%. These are explanatory reformulations, with no new theorem, proof, or substantive formal assumption.

C1.justification: The central minimalistic-framework and strong multi-class performance claims remain. v3's introduction explicitly emphasizes scalability and efficient downsizing, including large-model claims across all three original datasets. The abstract also changes its class-separated comparison from surpassing leading records to achieving them.

C2.justification: v3 adds an input-resolution fairness rationale and a medical-evaluation limitation concerning missing 3D context. It revises the pretraining interpretation from MIM-specific resolution problems and CL adaptability to broader image-level resolution sensitivity, with added discussion of MAE's weakness without fine-tuning. The original computational and sensory-versus-semantic limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 reports code as available rather than forthcoming, adds RD4AD adaptation details and new-dataset hyperparameters, and attributes most comparator results to ADer. However, it omits v1's explicit ViT-Large layer-selection and decoder-configuration guidance. This is a documentation loss, not evidence that those settings changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds classic denoising-autoencoder references, ADer and additional benchmark/application citations, and support from module-wise distillation research. The omni-frequency channel-selection reference is removed. These modestly expand the grounding while preserving the main positioning relative to earlier UAD and MUAD methods.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: MUAD related work moves into the main text; scaling and foundation analyses become prominent main-text material; dropout and reconstruction-constraint studies move to the appendix. The introduction and attention discussion are rewritten, supplementary sections are reorganized, and the author/affiliation block changes.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column layout with extensive table relocation and resizing. Figure 1 is rearranged, Figure 2 gains explicit layer-group annotations, and Figures 3–4 receive labeling or spacing edits. New comparison tables are added. The appendix anomaly-map images are identical but displayed larger.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens evidence about generality, input-size fairness, computational tradeoffs, and component portability through additional datasets and the new RD4AD and scaling experiments. These improve an already extensively evaluated core contribution. Benefits are tempered by lost scaling implementation details, removal of EfficientAD from Table 2, and a new reporting inconsistency: Table 5 gives default RD4AD image F1 as 96.1 while retained Table 1 gives 95.2.
